newsitem.title: USA: Yellow Freight says raises fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Yellow Freight says raises fuel surcharge.

text.p: Yellow Freight System said it increased its fuel surcharge on the cost of carrying freight by one-half a percentage point effective October 9 in response to rising diesel fuel prices.
Yellow Freight is a unit of Yellow Corp.

"The increase was triggered when fuel prices passed an index milestone of $1.30 per gallon. The change raised Yellow's surcharge from 1.5 to 2.0 percent of a shipper's transportation billing rates," the company said.
Yellow said it first imposed its surcharge on September 3, when the U.S. National Average Fuel Index was at $1.222 per gallon. The index reached $1.308 on Monday, it said.
Diesel fuel prices have increased about one percent per week for the past nine weeks, Yellow said.
"Yellow's surcharge will revert to 1.5 percent if the U.S. National Average Fuel Index, published every Monday, falls below $1.30 per gallon," the company said.
